- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent periods.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior high), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward prior range.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast weights.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates > 3% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day trend, not 30-day trend.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.10) and price is flat, model often predicts minor drift; reduce forecast volatility by 30–50% to avoid overfitting to noise.
